label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, A, B, B where the asset was D, B, D, A: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Handle and head outline read as a wrench with a head at one end, and the head is in proportion (about 7 of 18.4 units). But the head is a flat rectangular block in the left, top and below views, with no V-shaped toothed jaw face angled off the handle as a pipe wrench has. The brief's silhouette is a pipe wrench, so this is a shape fault in the head, not paint.

M2.reason: Measured long axis 18.4 against the 18 asked (sizeOff 0.02), well within the 15% band. Width 3.1 and height 10.7 are not checked against any brief figure.

M3.reason: The brief names a red handle worn to bare iron and a heavy toothed jaw. The handle is there in every side view: red sections with a dark bare-iron band in the middle and a steel end. The jaw has teeth: small square studs in two rows on the head (TOP and BELOW views), about 3 to 4 per row. Nothing the brief names is missing. The pivot and adjusting nut are not named, so their absence is not charged.

M4.reason: Red painted handle at both ends, a dark grey worn band mid-handle reading as bare iron, and a mid-grey steel head. This matches the brief's red handle worn to bare iron, with no colour the brief does not ask for.

M5.reason: The worn iron band on the handle, the bevelled panel lines and the dark patches on the head are all there, and nothing is smeared. The worn-to-iron wear the brief asks for is visible in the handle and in-hand views.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test as measured: in four readings of the four-model line-up, the asset was picked as the one not made by Valve each time it was not the odd one out, so it passed for one of the game's. Scored 2 as instructed.

M7.reason: The w_ model lies flat along its length on its origin, as a dropped weapon would. The brief gives no front, and nothing in the views contradicts an upright or lying placement.

M8.reason: SMAK checkErrors is empty. 186 triangles is under twice the Half-Life weapon median of 142 (284) and under twice the third quartile of 187 (374). No open or inside-out faces are visible in the sides and angle views.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the wrench sits lower than the game's crowbar, with the jaw block at the bottom of the frame and the handle rising up to a flared cap. The crowbar's hook is at the top and its handle runs down to the hand, so the wrench looks held the other way round, with its jaw where the hand would grip. The hands are not drawn in the picture, so the grip cannot be confirmed. In attack.png the weapon does not visibly leave the hands, since they are not seen.
